zh.title: 英语提分为什么要先解决词汇，而不是一上来刷卷子？
zh.description: 很多家长觉得单词可以自己背，但英语提分真正看的是词汇能不能转化到听力、阅读、写作和刷卷复盘。本文解释AI脑波英语为什么先测评、先解决音标和词汇，再做语法、听力、阅读、写作和刷卷。
zh.lead: 如果孩子单词不会读、听不出、认不准、写不出，一上来刷卷子往往只是重复丢分。英语提分的第一步，不是把孩子推向更多题，而是先看词汇底座能不能支撑听力、阅读、写作和考试题型。

sections.h2: 为什么很多家长低估了词汇对分数的影响？
paragraphs: 家长常说：单词不就是自己背吗？这句话只说对了一半。孩子当然可以自己背单词，但考试考的不是孩子有没有背过单词表，而是孩子能不能在题里认出来、听出来、写出来、用出来。
英语卷面上的很多失分，表面看是阅读错、听力错、完形错、作文写不出，底层经常是词汇没有真正打通。单词只停留在眼熟或中文意思，会让孩子在真实考试场景里反应慢、判断错、写不出。
bullets: 单词不会读，听力容易听不出来。
单词不认识，阅读题干和文章都容易卡住。
单词只背中文意思，完形、语境和搭配题仍然不会选。
单词不会拼，作文和句子输出会受限。
单词背了就忘，刷卷子会反复错同类问题。

sections.h2: 为什么不建议一开始就大量刷卷子？
paragraphs: 刷卷子本身没有错，但顺序很重要。如果孩子的词汇底座、音标自然拼读和基本句子理解都没有解决，刷卷子只能暴露问题，不能自动解决问题。
更合理的顺序是：先测孩子卡点，再补音标和自然拼读，快速突破目标词汇，然后把词汇放到语法、听力、阅读、写作和刷卷复盘里使用。这样刷卷才有意义。
bullets: 基础弱的孩子：先音标/自然拼读，再核心词汇，再基础语法和阅读。
中等生：先词汇集中突破，再补语法漏洞，再做阅读、完形、听力和写作专项。
冲刺生：先高频词和短语，再错题归因，再限时专项和整卷复盘。

sections.h2: AI脑波英语如何把词汇训练变成可检测结果？
paragraphs: AI脑波英语不是让孩子随便背一组词，也不是只让孩子进学习舱体验一下。标准流程应该是先测评、确定目标词、进舱前读熟、学习舱训练、出舱检测、错词复现和阶段复测。
检测重点不是一句“感觉不错”，而是看孩子训练前后是否真的发生变化。家长应关注会读数量、英译汉、汉译英、拼写、听音辨词和次日复现。
bullets: 进舱前：目标词先读熟，明显读错的词先标记。
训练中：学习舱完成目标词输入，教练观察学生状态。
出舱后：做英译汉、汉译英、拼写和听音辨词。
复现后：错词进入复现清单，次日或隔日再测。

sections.h2: 词汇突破后，后续服务怎么衔接？
paragraphs: 词汇是底座，但不是终点。真正的提分服务要把词汇继续转化到题型和卷面结果中。词汇突破后，孩子还需要语法补漏洞、听力抓关键词、阅读定位与长难句拆解、写作句型和素材训练，以及刷卷后的错题归因。
这也是为什么AI脑波英语的服务标准里要同时包含音标、词汇、语法、听力、阅读、写作和刷卷复盘。只背单词不转化，分数提升会不稳定；只刷卷不补底座，孩子会越来越焦虑。
bullets: 语法：补孩子试卷和阅读中真实暴露的小漏洞。
听力：把词汇转为听音辨词、场景词和关键词定位。
阅读/完形：用词汇、短语和长难句拆解提升题型得分。
写作：把词汇转化成句子、段落和限时作文。
刷卷：先专项，再模块，再整卷，最后错题回炉。

sections.h2: 9.9元体验200词适合家长验证什么？
paragraphs: 石家庄当前主推的9.9元体验200词，不应该被理解成低价噱头，而是一种低门槛验证方式。200个词足够看出孩子会不会读、能不能认、能不能听、能不能拼、第二天还能不能复现。
家长可以用一次体验判断：孩子的问题是不是卡在词汇底座，孩子对学习舱训练是否接受，出舱检测是否能看到变化，以及后续是否值得进入系统训练。
bullets: 体验前看基础：会读多少、认识多少。
体验后看检测：英译汉、汉译英、拼写、听辨。
隔天看复现：有没有明显遗忘。
最终看路径：是否需要继续做词汇、语法、阅读、听力、写作和刷卷复盘。

faqs.q: 单词真的不能自己背吗？
faqs.a: 可以自己背，但很多孩子的问题不是没有背，而是不会读、听不出、拼不准、不会在题里用。AI脑波英语训练的是词汇从记忆到考试应用的完整链条。
如果词汇底座不稳，刷题只是不断暴露同类问题。先把音标、自然拼读和核心词汇解决，再做语法、阅读、听力、写作和刷卷复盘，提分路径更清楚。
主要看孩子训练前后是否有可检测变化，包括会读、会认、会听、会拼和复现情况，而不是只看孩子是否觉得新鲜。

faqs.q: 词汇突破后还需要学语法和阅读吗？
faqs.a: 需要。词汇是底座，后续还要通过语法、听力、阅读、写作和刷卷复盘，把词汇转化成题型得分和考试表现。

zh.cta: 如果孩子英语拖总分、单词背了就忘、阅读听力写作都受影响，建议先预约30分钟测评，再决定是否做9.9元体验200词。

en.title: Why Vocabulary Should Come Before More Practice Papers in English Score Improvement
en.description: Parents often think students can memorize vocabulary alone. This article explains why vocabulary must become usable in listening, reading, writing and paper review before practice papers can produce better results.
en.lead: If students cannot read, recognize, hear, spell and recall words, doing more practice papers often repeats the same mistakes. English score improvement usually needs vocabulary diagnosis before large-volume test drilling.

sections.h2: Why do parents often underestimate vocabulary?
paragraphs: Many parents say vocabulary is something students can memorize by themselves. That is only partly true. Exams do not test whether a student has looked at a word list. They test whether the student can recognize words in reading, hear them in listening, use them in writing and understand them in context.
A weak vocabulary base can appear as reading mistakes, listening mistakes, cloze mistakes or poor writing. The visible problem may be the paper, but the deeper cause is often unstable vocabulary use.
bullets: If words cannot be read, listening becomes harder.
If words cannot be recognized, reading slows down.
If words are only memorized as Chinese meanings, context questions remain difficult.
If spelling is weak, writing output is limited.
If words fade quickly, practice papers repeat the same errors.

sections.h2: Why not start with more practice papers?
paragraphs: Practice papers are useful, but timing matters. If phonics, vocabulary and sentence understanding are weak, more papers expose the problem without necessarily solving it.
A better sequence is assessment first, then phonics and pronunciation repair, focused vocabulary training, grammar repair, listening, reading, writing and finally structured paper review.
bullets: Weak foundation: phonics first, then core vocabulary and basic grammar.
Middle-level learners: vocabulary breakthrough, then reading, cloze, listening and writing transfer.
Exam-stage learners: high-frequency words, phrases, error analysis and timed paper review.

sections.h2: How does AI Brainwave English make vocabulary measurable?
paragraphs: AI Brainwave English should not be understood as a simple word-list product or a mysterious learning cabin experience. The useful part is the full loop: assessment, target words, pre-cabin reading, learning-cabin input, exit testing, error review and follow-up recall.
Parents should not only ask how many words were covered. They should ask how many words the student could read, translate, spell, hear and recall after the session and again later.
bullets: Before the cabin: read and prepare target words.
During the session: complete focused vocabulary input with coach observation.
After the session: test translation, spelling and audio recognition.
During review: retest error words and track recall.

paragraphs: Vocabulary is the base, not the finish line. After vocabulary improves, students still need grammar repair, listening keyword practice, reading and cloze strategy, writing sentence output and paper-review routines.

This is why the AI Brainwave English service standard includes phonics, vocabulary, grammar, listening, reading, writing and practice-paper review. Vocabulary without transfer is unstable; paper drilling without foundation increases frustration.
bullets: Grammar: repair small gaps that appear in real papers and reading passages.
Listening: turn words into sound recognition and keyword positioning.
Reading and cloze: connect words, phrases and sentence structure to question types.
Writing: turn vocabulary into sentences, paragraphs and timed output.
Paper review: use error attribution before doing more full papers.

paragraphs: A 200-word trial is not just a low-price offer. It can be used as a small diagnostic window. Two hundred target words are enough to see whether the student can read, recognize, hear, spell and recall words after training.

For local teams, the trial should show parents the before-and-after difference and help decide whether the student needs a larger vocabulary, grammar, reading, listening, writing and paper-review plan.
bullets: Before: check how many target words the student can read and recognize.
After: test translation, spelling and listening recognition.
Next day: check recall and error words.
Decision: decide whether a systematic training path is appropriate.

faqs.q: Can students memorize vocabulary by themselves?
faqs.a: Yes, but many students do not only need more memorization. They need accurate reading, sound recognition, spelling, recall and transfer into reading, listening and writing.

faqs.q: Why should vocabulary come before more practice papers?
faqs.a: If the vocabulary base is weak, practice papers repeat the same mistakes. Vocabulary training gives later grammar, reading, listening, writing and paper review a stronger foundation.
It can test whether the learner can read, recognize, translate, spell, hear and recall target words before and after a focused session.

faqs.q: Does vocabulary training replace grammar and reading?
faqs.a: No. Vocabulary is the base. A complete service should still include grammar, listening, reading, writing and practice-paper review.

en.cta: If a student keeps forgetting vocabulary or cannot transfer words into reading, listening and writing, start with assessment before choosing a larger training path.
